title: Introduce hierarchical smoke-sampler and late-fail attenuator CI hook
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds hierarchical smoke-sampler to prioritize prompt cohorts by disruption score; introduces late-fail attenuator CI hook to avoid escalating one-off intermittent failures while still surfacing persistent regressions; includes unit+integration tests and docs; rollout behind feature flag; no immediate production gating change unless enabled.
description: Motivation: intermittent prompt-set failures (spikes driven by small cohorts) are causing noisy CI alerts and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR adds a hierarchical smoke-sampler that builds a two-tier sampling plan (cohort-level followed by intra-cohort sampling) to increase coverage of high-variance prompt families while keeping smoke evaluation budgets bounded. It also introduces a late-fail attenuator CI hook that downweights isolated failures that occur late in a sliding window and only escalates when failure weight persists across windows. Design: sampler computes cohort disruption scores using historical eval variance and recent error-rate deltas; top-K cohorts are sampled proportionally to disruption with a minimum floor to avoid starvation. The attenuator consumes per-prompt failure history and a tunable half-life to compute an effective failure weight; single-window blips are suppressed, sustained deviations trigger the existing quality gate. Rollout plan: feature-flagged in CI config, dry-run for two weeks producing annotation-only reports, then opt-in for branch protection gating. Tests: unit tests for sampler statistics, integration scenario with synthetic prompt drift, end-to-end CI scenario recorded in artifacts. Checklist: implement sampler and hook, add feature flag, tests, docs and examples, update alerting thresholds. Impact: should reduce noisy false positives and improve signal-to-noise for real regressions. Backwards compatibility: disabled by default; no breaking changes.
